cards.statement: A client can read its own Azure Cosmos DB writes with Session consistency and the relevant session token.
cards.explanation: Session consistency uses the latest token for the relevant items as a minimum version barrier, so the client's reads include its prior writes.

source.title: Consistency level choices in Azure Cosmos DB

cards.statement: Azure Cosmos DB supports Strong consistency in an account configured for multiple write regions.
cards.explanation: Azure Cosmos DB excludes Strong consistency from accounts with multiple write regions. A design using multiple write regions selects a weaker consistency level.
cards.misconception: Strong consistency is compatible with an Azure Cosmos DB account that accepts writes in multiple regions.

source.title: Consistency level choices in Azure Cosmos DB

cards.statement: RU-based Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB supports multi-document transactions across shards of a sharded collection.
cards.explanation: RU-based Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB limits multi-document transactions to a single unsharded collection. Cross-shard transactions need a different design.
cards.misconception: RU-based Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB preserves MongoDB transaction support across shards.
cards.volatilityNote: Supported MongoDB API transaction capabilities can expand as the service evolves.

source.title: Supported features and syntax in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB 6.0 server version

cards.statement: Azure Cosmos DB's integrated cache can reduce RU use for repeated point reads routed through a dedicated gateway.
cards.explanation: Repeated point reads served from the integrated cache avoid backend RU charges. Cache reuse is the cost lever for a read-heavy workload.

source.title: Integrated cache in Azure Cosmos DB

cards.statement: Azure Data Lake Storage gives analytics jobs atomic directory renames when the account uses a hierarchical namespace.
cards.explanation: A hierarchical namespace changes a directory entry during a rename instead of processing its blobs individually, reducing the work needed to publish analytics output.

source.title: Azure Data Lake Storage hierarchical namespace

cards.statement: Azure Files serves SMB and NFS clients simultaneously through the same share when a workload needs both protocols.
cards.explanation: An Azure file share uses SMB or NFS. Workloads needing both protocols use separate shares, even when the shares reside in the same storage account.
cards.misconception: An Azure file share can expose the same files concurrently through SMB and NFS.

source.title: Plan an Azure Files deployment

cards.statement: Azure Files provisioned v2 bills for provisioned storage capacity even when a share uses less space.
cards.explanation: Provisioned v2 charges for the capacity an architect provisions rather than the space files consume. Unused provisioned capacity remains a cost dimension.

source.title: Understand Azure Files billing

cards.statement: Microsoft recommends RA-GZRS for storage accounts needing maximum availability and durability.
cards.explanation: RA-GZRS keeps a geographically separate copy for regional recovery, matching Microsoft's maximum availability and durability guidance.
cards.volatilityNote: Microsoft's recommended redundancy choice can change as storage options evolve.

source.title: Azure storage disaster recovery planning and failover

cards.statement: Azure Table storage lets an architect add native secondary indexes for frequent non-key lookups.
cards.explanation: Azure Table storage indexes the partition and row keys. For other frequent lookup paths, the application maintains alternate entities or its own index entities.
cards.misconception: Azure Table storage offers native secondary indexes on arbitrary entity properties.

source.title: Design Azure Table storage for queries

cards.statement: Azure Blob Storage blocks an app from creating a new version when an earlier version has an immutability policy.
cards.explanation: Version-level immutability protects the selected version. An application can write a new version of the blob while the earlier protected version remains intact.
cards.misconception: Immutability on a blob version freezes future writes to the blob's version history.

source.title: Data protection overview

cards.statement: Azure Blob Storage lets a logging app add records to an immutable append blob with protected append writes enabled.
cards.explanation: Protected append writes permit new blocks at the end of an append blob while preserving its immutability. Existing blocks remain protected from changes.

source.title: Container-level WORM policies for immutable blob data

cards.statement: Azure Blob Storage releases a legal hold when the compliance team's retention interval expires.
cards.explanation: A legal hold remains in effect until an authorized user explicitly clears it. It suits retention whose end date is unknown.
cards.misconception: A legal hold expires on a scheduled retention deadline.

source.title: Immutable storage for blob data overview

cards.statement: A private on-premises data source can feed Azure Data Factory copy activity through a self-hosted integration runtime.
cards.explanation: A self-hosted integration runtime runs inside the private network and moves data between reachable private sources and cloud stores.

source.title: Integration runtime in Azure Data Factory

cards.statement: A self-hosted integration runtime lets Azure Data Factory run mapping data flow transformations on its host.
cards.explanation: Azure Data Factory executes mapping data flows on managed Spark clusters supplied by the Azure integration runtime.
cards.misconception: A self-hosted integration runtime executes mapping data flows locally.

source.title: Integration runtime in Azure Data Factory

cards.statement: Azure Data Factory managed private endpoints let its pipelines privately access approved Azure Storage accounts.
cards.explanation: Azure Data Factory managed private endpoints reach supported stores over Azure's backbone after the resource owner approves the connection.

source.title: Azure Data Factory managed virtual network and managed private endpoints

cards.statement: An Azure Data Factory schedule trigger can backfill missed time intervals when an ingestion pipeline resumes.
cards.explanation: Azure Data Factory uses tumbling window triggers for historical backfill. Schedule triggers handle current or future runs.
cards.misconception: Schedule triggers retain missed intervals for historical backfill.

source.title: Pipeline execution and triggers in Azure Data Factory or Azure Synapse Analytics

cards.statement: Azure Data Factory can use a saved watermark to copy new or updated database rows between successive extraction runs.
cards.explanation: Azure Data Factory reads rows between the previous and current watermark values. A timestamp that advances when a row changes makes the pattern suitable for incremental updates.

source.title: Incrementally load data into Azure Data Factory or Synapse Analytics

cards.statement: Azure Synapse Analytics lets dedicated SQL pool queries continue uninterrupted during a compute scaling operation.
cards.explanation: Azure Synapse Analytics cancels dedicated SQL pool queries when scaling is requested and rolls back open transactions before changing compute resources.
cards.misconception: Dedicated SQL pool compute scaling preserves query execution.

source.title: Manage compute in a dedicated SQL pool

cards.statement: Azure Synapse Analytics automatically stops compute charges when an architect pauses a dedicated SQL pool.
cards.explanation: Pausing an Azure Synapse Analytics dedicated SQL pool releases its compute resources. Storage charges continue for the retained data.

source.title: Manage compute in a dedicated SQL pool

cards.statement: Azure Synapse Analytics serverless SQL pool lets analysts explore lake files directly in their existing storage.
cards.explanation: Azure Synapse Analytics serverless SQL pool reads lake data where it resides, avoiding a prerequisite load into a dedicated warehouse.

source.title: Serverless SQL pool in Azure Synapse Analytics

cards.statement: Azure Stream Analytics queries Azure SQL Database reference data afresh upon arrival of an incoming event.
cards.explanation: Azure Stream Analytics joins events against an in-memory snapshot of Azure SQL Database reference data. It refreshes that snapshot at a configured interval.
cards.misconception: Azure SQL Database reference joins retrieve live database values for each event.

source.title: Use reference data for lookups in Stream Analytics

cards.statement: Azure Data Explorer automatically reprocesses pre-existing source rows when an architect creates an update policy.
cards.explanation: Azure Data Explorer update policies react to newly ingested data. An architect handles existing source rows through a separate backfill.
cards.misconception: Creating an update policy retroactively transforms existing source data.

source.title: Update policy overview

cards.statement: Azure Synapse Analytics lets Spark jobs finish while autoscale decommissions nodes during a scale-in operation.
cards.explanation: Azure Synapse Analytics marks scale-in candidates for decommissioning, then lets running Spark jobs finish before removing the nodes.

source.title: Automatically scale Azure Synapse Analytics Apache Spark pools

cards.statement: Fabric Data Warehouse can persist analytical tables in SQL Server's native database file format for sharing.
cards.explanation: Fabric Data Warehouse stores tables in Delta format: Parquet data files with a transaction log. This format supports sharing data across analytical tools.
cards.misconception: Fabric Data Warehouse uses SQL Server database files because it offers a SQL Database Engine surface.
cards.volatilityNote: Microsoft Fabric is evolving rapidly; its storage architecture and interoperability options may change.

source.title: What is Fabric Data Warehouse?

cards.statement: For on-premises VMware recovery, Azure Site Recovery's latest processed point favors shorter recovery time.
cards.explanation: The latest processed recovery point skips processing replicated data that is still pending, reducing failover time when restoring an on-premises VMware VM.

source.title: Run VMware VMs failover to Azure

cards.statement: Azure Site Recovery recovery plans can invoke Azure Automation runbooks to coordinate application recovery.
cards.explanation: A recovery plan can run Azure Automation runbooks during failover to Azure, automating application-specific tasks that would otherwise slow recovery.

source.title: About recovery plans

cards.statement: Azure Site Recovery shuts down the primary site when a recovery plan runs a test failover for an on-premises app.
cards.explanation: A recovery plan's test failover leaves the primary site running. This lets a team validate an on-premises application's recovery while production continues.
cards.misconception: Disaster recovery drills shut down the production site like a real failover.

source.title: About recovery plans

cards.statement: Azure Backup administrators can disable vault immutability after they lock its immutable setting.
cards.explanation: Locking an Azure Backup vault's immutability setting makes it irreversible, preventing administrators or attackers from switching off that protection.
cards.misconception: An administrator can reverse a locked immutability setting.

source.title: Immutable vault for Azure Backup

cards.statement: An immutable vault in Azure Backup protects operational blob backups from destructive changes.
cards.explanation: Azure Backup vault immutability excludes operational blob backups. Its protection applies to recovery points held in the vault, rather than operational recovery points.
cards.misconception: Vault immutability extends to operational blob recovery points.

source.title: Immutable vault for Azure Backup

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database point-in-time restore can rewind the original database to undo an application's data corruption.
cards.explanation: Point-in-time restore creates a new Azure SQL Database. An administrator then decides how to use the restored database to recover the application.
cards.misconception: Point-in-time restore overwrites the original database in place.

source.title: Restore a database from a backup in Azure SQL Database

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database long-term retention backups remain available after an administrator deletes the logical server.
cards.explanation: Azure SQL Database retains long-term retention backups after logical-server deletion. Administrators can restore them to another server in the same subscription.

source.title: Long-term retention backups

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database geo-restore depends on available target-region capacity at the time of recovery.
cards.explanation: Geo-restore provisions a database from geo-replicated backups when requested. A regional disaster can increase demand, so available target-region capacity affects recovery.

source.title: Restore a database from a backup in Azure SQL Database

cards.statement: Azure Cosmos DB continuous backup automatically protects a single-region account against regional disaster.
cards.explanation: Azure Cosmos DB continuous backups need another account region for resilience against regional disaster. Enabling continuous backup alone does not provide that protection.
cards.misconception: Continuous backup automatically places recoverable copies outside a single account region.

source.title: Continuous backup with point-in-time restore in Azure Cosmos DB

cards.statement: Blob soft delete lets administrators recover blobs after an application deletes their containing container.
cards.explanation: Blob soft delete protects individual blobs, rather than a deleted container. Container soft delete is the feature that recovers a deleted container and its contents.
cards.misconception: Blob soft delete covers deletion of the enclosing container.

source.title: Data protection overview

cards.statement: Azure Files vaulted backups can recover a share after the source share and its snapshots become unavailable.
cards.explanation: Azure Files vaulted backups keep offsite recovery data. Azure Backup can restore the share to an alternate location even when the source snapshots are unavailable.

source.title: About Azure Files backup

cards.statement: Azure Storage automatically retains geo-redundancy after a customer-managed planned failover to the secondary region.
cards.explanation: Customer-managed planned failover leaves the storage account geo-redundant as GRS. The original primary becomes the new secondary, retaining a geographically separate copy.

source.title: Azure storage disaster recovery planning and failover

cards.statement: Azure automatically recreates a zonal virtual machine in a healthy zone when its original zone fails.
cards.explanation: A zonal Azure virtual machine remains tied to its zone. Customers design redundant capacity in other zones instead of relying on automatic cross-zone recreation.
cards.misconception: Azure automatically replaces standalone zonal virtual machines in another zone during a zone outage.

source.title: Reliability in Azure Virtual Machines

cards.statement: Azure App Service automatically attempts to replace lost instances after a zone fails in a zone-redundant plan.
cards.explanation: App Service backfills instances on a best-effort basis during a zone outage. A capacity requirement that survives zone loss calls for provisioning spare capacity ahead of time.

source.title: Reliability in Azure App Service

cards.statement: Shared zone-redundant Azure managed disks support clustered virtual machines in different availability zones.
cards.explanation: A shared ZRS managed disk connects cluster nodes across zones, so the surviving node can take over the shared storage when the primary node's zone fails.

source.title: Redundancy options for managed disks

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database failover groups let applications reuse listener addresses after a geo-failover.
cards.explanation: Failover-group listener names stay fixed while Azure updates their DNS targets. An application reconnects through the same listener address.

source.title: Failover groups overview & best practices - Azure SQL Database

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database forced failover can lose primary writes still awaiting geo-replication.
cards.explanation: Forced failover promotes the geo-secondary before pending replication completes. Recent primary writes may therefore be lost.

source.title: Failover groups overview & best practices - Azure SQL Database

cards.statement: A Business Critical secondary created by an Azure SQL Database failover group automatically inherits zone redundancy.
cards.explanation: A failover group creates a Business Critical secondary with zone redundancy disabled by default. Configure that secondary's zone redundancy separately.
cards.misconception: Failover groups propagate a Business Critical primary's zone-redundancy setting to a newly created secondary.
cards.volatilityNote: Default propagation of zone-redundancy settings when Azure creates a secondary may change.

source.title: Failover groups overview & best practices - Azure SQL Database

cards.statement: Microsoft recommends Microsoft-managed failover policy for Azure SQL Database failover groups.
cards.explanation: Microsoft recommends customer-managed policy so the customer controls when to fail over an affected group.
cards.misconception: Microsoft recommends delegating Azure SQL Database failover decisions to the service.

source.title: Failover groups overview & best practices - Azure SQL Database

cards.statement: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server can serve reporting queries from its high availability standby.
cards.explanation: The flexible server HA standby stays in recovery mode until promotion and rejects application read queries. Reporting needs a separate read-serving design.
cards.misconception: The PostgreSQL high availability standby also provides reporting capacity.
tags: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server

source.title: High availability in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server

cards.statement: Azure SQL Managed Instance failover groups replicate all user databases in an instance as one failover unit.
cards.explanation: A Managed Instance failover group covers the instance's user databases together. This scope matters when applications need independent database failover boundaries.

source.title: Failover groups overview & best practices - Azure SQL Managed Instance

cards.statement: Azure Cosmos DB commits writes locally in a satellite region of a multi-region write account.
cards.explanation: A satellite region acknowledges writes after a local quorum commits them. Azure Cosmos DB sends them to the hub asynchronously for conflict resolution.

source.title: Multi-region writes in Azure Cosmos DB

cards.statement: Read-access geo-redundant Azure Storage supports outage reads guaranteed to include the latest primary writes.
cards.explanation: Azure Storage replicates asynchronously to its read-access secondary. Applications using that endpoint during an outage need to tolerate data that trails the primary.
cards.misconception: Secondary-region read access provides the latest primary-region writes during an outage.

source.title: Data redundancy - Azure Storage

cards.statement: Azure Files can serve reads from a geo-redundant account's secondary region before account failover.
cards.explanation: Geo-redundant Azure file shares become accessible in the secondary region after account failover. Read-access storage redundancy does not expose a secondary file-share endpoint.
cards.misconception: A geo-redundant account makes its secondary Azure file shares readable before failover.

source.title: Data redundancy in Azure Files
